In [[geometry]], the '''metabiaugmented dodecahedron''' is one of the [[Johnson solid]]s ({{math|''J''{{sub|60}}}}). It can be viewed as a [[dodecahedron]] with two [[pentagonal pyramid]]s ({{math|''J''{{sub|2}}}}) attached to two faces that are separated by one face. (The two faces are not opposite, but not adjacent either.) When pyramids are attached to a dodecahedron in other ways, they may result in an [[augmented dodecahedron]] ({{math|''J''{{sub|58}}}}), a [[parabiaugmented dodecahedron]] ({{math|''J''{{sub|59}}}}), a [[triaugmented dodecahedron]] ({{math|''J''{{sub|61}}}}), or even a [[pentakis dodecahedron]] if the faces are made to be irregular.
